content.value_statement: Python projects often need stronger correctness, types, and style. This skill guides implementation and review using practical Python best practices.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Python code for mutable defaults, bare except clauses, resource leaks, and style issues.
Guides use of type hints, dataclasses, generics, and documented interfaces.
Recommends context managers, list comprehensions, generators, and standard library tools.
Provides Google-style docstring patterns and structured review output.
Helps debug Python exceptions and improve edge case handling.
limitations: Does not execute tests or verify runtime behavior by itself.
Does not replace domain-specific security review for production systems.
Guidance is limited to Python best practices described in the skill files.
Needs project context to choose performance tradeoffs accurately.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Find Python correctness, typing, error handling, performance, and documentation issues before merge.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Script
use_cases.description: Improve an existing script with clearer functions, safer resource handling, and better style.

use_cases.title: Learn Python Practices
use_cases.description: Understand common Python pitfalls through concise examples and review checklists.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Quality Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small function or script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Python code for mutable defaults, bare except clauses, missing type hints, and unclear names. Explain each issue simply.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Function Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me improve this Python function interface with type hints, a clear docstring, input validation, and specific exceptions.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor for Maintainability
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refactor of a module or workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Python module for readability, data containers, resource cleanup, and performance without changing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Python
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release-focused Python review. Prioritize correctness, error handling, type safety, resource cleanup, performance, tests, and documentation.

output_examples.input: Review this utility module for Python quality.
output: Critical issue: one function uses a mutable default list, which can leak state between calls.
High priority: several public functions lack return type annotations and clear error behavior.
Medium priority: the module needs shorter names and clearer docstrings for public helpers.
Recommendation: use a dataclass because the class mainly stores typed fields.
Add explicit field types, defaults, and immutability when the object should not change.
Keep custom methods only for behavior that dataclasses do not provide automatically.

output_examples.input: Make this file processing script safer.
output: Use context managers for every file handle so cleanup happens after errors.
Handle expected parsing and missing-file exceptions separately.
Add tests for empty files, invalid input, and large input streams.

best_practices: Address correctness issues before style changes or performance tuning.
Use specific exceptions and explain fallback behavior clearly.
Add type hints and docstrings to public functions that other users call.
anti_patterns: Do not use mutable default arguments for lists, dictionaries, or sets.
Do not hide errors with bare except clauses or silent pass statements.
Do not optimize Python code before measuring the actual bottleneck.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps write, review, debug, and improve Python code using practical quality guidelines.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify correctness, type safety, error handling, performance, style, and documentation issues.

faq.question: Does it run Python tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and review output, but test execution depends on the host agent and project setup.

faq.question: Is it useful for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common Python mistakes with simple examples and clear fixes.

faq.question: Does it cover security?
faq.answer: It includes basic checks such as input validation and unsafe operations, but it is not a full security audit skill.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
